title: Dynamic tranche prioritizer and variable-fill compactor for prefill/decoder scheduling
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: Our current runtime groups incoming requests into fixed-length buckets which leads to excessive padding for long-tail sequences and suboptimal kernel choices during decode. This increases per-token cost and worsens P95 latency under mixed workloads.

Goal: Implement a runtime component (Tranche Prioritizer + Variable-Fill Compactor) that dynamically assigns new requests into transient tranches based on predicted remaining decode length and kernel affinity, and compacts micro-batches by selectively filling slots with compatible short sequences or prefills to reduce padding. The system should: reduce effective padding by >=20% on average for mixed seqlen traffic, improve P95 decode latency by >=10% for 99th-percentile microburst windows, and maintain or improve throughput.

Approach: 1) Add a lightweight seqlen-estimator at ingestion (reuse existing prefix-length predictor model) and a kernel-affinity heuristic (simple model-to-kernel mapping + runtime cost-estimates). 2) Maintain multiple transient tranches per worker (e.g., short/med/long/latency-sensitive) with policies for prefill prioritization and slot compaction. 3) When a new request arrives, attempt to compact it into a partially-filled microbatch by evicting low-priority placeholders or swapping compatible prefills; otherwise, place it into the best-fit tranche. 4) During decode, prefer kernels with lower overhead for the tranche; fall back to universal kernels when necessary.

Non-goals: Full model re-training for length prediction, end-to-end routing across regions, or replacing KV cache mechanics. This iteration focuses on on-node scheduling and batching heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Integration tests exercising tranche assignment under synthetic mixed-length traffic
Benchmark: end-to-end P95 decode latency improvement >=10% on microburst workload (internal benchmark suite)
Benchmark: average padding token reduction >=20% across 24h real traffic sample in staging
No regression in throughput for long-steady-stream scenarios (+/-3%)
Telemetry: new tranche-level metrics emitted (tranche_fill_rate, tranche_evictions, tranche_kernel_affinity) and dashboards created in Console
design_decisions: Use an estimator (stateless RPC to prediction cache) instead of an expensive model call at ingress to keep latency low
Bound number of tranches per worker to 4 to limit scheduling complexity and head-of-line blocking
Eviction policy favors removing placeholder prefill slots with lowest predicted continuation probability
Prefer kernel-affinity hints for prefill scheduling but allow runtime fallback to universal kernels to ensure availability
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Misclassification of sequence length causing fragmentation -> Mitigation: conservative tranche thresholds and opportunistic slot compaction within a short timeout window (50ms)
Risk: Increased scheduler CPU -> Mitigation: implement heuristics in C++ hot path with cheap integer ops and offload heavy scoring to background thread
Risk: KV cache incompatibility when swapping prefills -> Mitigation: only compact requests whose KV compatibility hash matches; otherwise avoid swapping

2026-03-04 Design feedback (Leah Kim): Request UI/telemetry contract for new tranche metrics and an experimental toggle per-cluster in the Console. Leah suggests exposing 'latency_sensitive' label on request tokens.

2026-03-06 Performance note (bench team): With kernel-affinity enabled, warm-start kernels reduced per-token CPU by ~9% for medium sequences; however cold-start penalty for long sequences increased decode wall time for single-request traces. Trade-off captured in decision log.

2026-03-08 Mateo Alvarez: Implemented compact swap guard to ensure KV-hash compatibility. Added unit tests and microbench harness. Running staging soak in us-west-2. Staging PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9278

2026-03-09 Ops: Staging telemetry shows tranche_evictions spike during a 30s burst; investigating whether tranche window parameter (50ms) is too small for high QPS. Lowered eviction aggressiveness in experiment 3.
